name: UCO Bank
title: UCO Bank - 532505 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Strong FY26 beat on credit growth (19.44% vs 12-15% guide) and asset quality (GNPA 2.17%, credit cost 0.62%), but FY27 guidance held at 12-14% and CD ratio rising toward 80-82%, so the supply-side read is pricing discipline on corporate loans, not capacity expansion.

triggers.label: Credit growth guide held at 12-14%
triggers.quote: guidance continues in the same range, looking at all scenarios

credit growth guidance was 12 to 15%, and our actual achievement is 19.44%

evasions.quote: We asked PLI to scale 4 above for the employees, which could not be paid this year because of certain reasons.

summary.headline: UCO Bank FY26 net profit rose 13.21% to Rs 2,768 crore; gross NPA fell to 2.17%, and FY27 guidance was held at 12-14% credit growth.
summary.overview: UCO Bank reported strong FY26 results, with gross advances up 19.44% YoY against 12-15% guidance and deposits up 11.59%. Asset quality improved, with gross NPA at 2.17% (down 52 bps), net NPA at 0.27%, and PCR at 97.79%. Management held FY27 guidance broadly unchanged despite analyst concern over the West Asia conflict, and said it holds about Rs 1,900 crore of provisioning buffers. Treasury was negative in Q4 due to MTM losses on AFS and HFT books.

segments.name: RAM (retail, agri, MSME)
segments.commentary: RAM advances grew 24%+ YoY, with retail up 26%+, agriculture up 26% and MSME up 19%. RAM share of book was 65%, against a 61-63% target.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Housing loans grew about 19% and car loans about 71%. Retail gold loans stood at about Rs 5,400 crore, and the 'others' bucket grew about 40% YoY, mainly on gold loans.

segments.name: Agriculture gold loans
segments.commentary: Agri gold loan book is about Rs 12,200 crore, so total gold loans are about Rs 18,000 crore at an estimated 8.5-9% yield.

segments.name: Treasury
segments.commentary: Q4 treasury income was negative Rs 16 crore versus about Rs 130 crore in Q3, after a Rs 135 crore MTM hit on the AFS book. Management cited a Rs 848 crore treasury segment profit against Rs 557 crore, which it said it would clarify offline.

guidance_outlook: FY27 deposit growth 10-12%, credit growth 12-14% (unchanged on deposits, credit range held at 12-14%).
FY27 CASA 37-38%; RAM share raised to 62-65%; CD ratio 80-82%.
FY27 credit cost below 0.75%; global NIM 2.8-2.9%.
FY27 gross NPA below 2%, net NPA below 0.2%, slippage ratio below 1%.
FY27 recovery and upgradation target Rs 2,000-2,500 crore.
ROA of 0.87% in FY26; management expects 0.95-1% by end of FY27.
FY27 IT budget above Rs 1,000 crore, following Rs 899 crore spend in FY26.
capex_capacity: Network: 3,412 domestic branches plus 2 overseas branches (Hong Kong, Singapore) and 1 representative office in Iran; 110 branches added in FY26; 61% of domestic branches in rural and semi-urban areas.
IT spend rose from Rs 576 crore (FY24) to Rs 642 crore (FY25) and Rs 899 crore (FY26).
Completed: CBDC app on iOS and Android, Murex treasury, Kolkata data centre consolidation, API gateway, ALM TPM automation, MuleHunter integration.

Planned for FY27: omnichannel mobile banking, cash management, supply chain finance, RPA, forex and prepaid cards, document management, e-notes, identity access management, Kolkata DR, centralised forex processing, and a CASA back office.
QIP approved by the Board, but management will seek shareholder approval at the AGM first and will not launch it this quarter.
demand_pricing: Corporate pipeline of about Rs 14,000 crore, but disbursement is held back by pricing; management said it will not grow corporate credit at the cost of margins.
Demand is coming from renewables, data centres, smart metering and road projects.
AAA-rated exposure is about 33% of the book (unchanged YoY); AA exposure fell to 26% from 29%.
About 65% of the loan book is linked to the repo rate; retail and MSME make up over Rs 1.1 lakh crore of the book.
CD ratio rose to 80.21% from the 75-77% target, which led the bank to push deposit mobilisation, with a focus on retail term deposits, savings and current accounts.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 guidance (credit growth of 12-14%) a sign that the West Asia conflict is weighing on the bank, and is SMA 1 rising stress for MSMEs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the guidance is conservative and has been 12-14% for three years while actual credit growth was 16% in FY24, 17.72% in FY25 and 19.44% in FY26. It attributed the rise in SMA 1 (to Rs 651 crore from Rs 260 crore) to the February 28-day effect rather than stress, and said total SMA 0-2 is 0.45% of standard advances.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs fall to Rs 182 crore from Rs 278 crore QoQ, and what buffers exist against ECL and the Labour Code?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the drop reflects a Rs 260 crore PLI provision in FY25, of which only about Rs 100 crore was paid in FY26, leaving about Rs 160 crore provided. It said it holds an ECL provision of Rs 1,038 crore, a Rs 341 crore contingency provision, and a Rs 530 crore COVID provision, for about Rs 1,900 crore of total buffers.

qa_highlights.question: Given the share price and the Rs 1,900 crore buffer, will the bank raise capital this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no plans to raise capital this quarter. It will seek AGM approval first and then launch the QIP at an opportune time when markets support it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost-to-income drop driven by, and what is the outlook for ROA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited fee income growth of 32% QoQ and 25% YoY, and tighter control of controllable costs, with recoveries from written-off accounts at about Rs 1,300 crore in FY26 against Rs 2,400-2,500 crore a year earlier. It expects ROA to reach 0.95-1% by end of FY27, from 0.87% now.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the West Asia war on MSMEs, and what share is covered by CGTMSE?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has not seen a major impact, with MSME slippages flat QoQ and no sharp rise in SMA. About 40% of advances are covered under CGTMSE.

qa_highlights.question: Why was treasury negative and what is the AFS reserve position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 treasury income was negative Rs 16 crore versus about Rs 130 crore in Q3, after a Rs 135 crore AFS MTM hit as yields rose above 7%. Yields have since eased to 6.95-6.98%, and AFS reserves stood at negative Rs 140 crore at March 2026.

risks_watch: Corporate loan growth could stay subdued while pricing discipline holds back disbursements from the Rs 14,000 crore pipeline.
The West Asia conflict may weigh on MSMEs; watch SMA 1 and SMA 2 buckets and MSME slippages in Q1 FY27.
Bond yields and treasury MTM could swing again; FY26 AFS reserves were negative Rs 140 crore.
Employee costs could rise when the Rs 160 crore residual PLI provision is paid, and the Labour Code effect is not yet quantified.
Deposit growth may lag credit growth (11.59% vs 19.44%), which keeps CD ratio pressure on margins; watch whether bulk deposits rise.
Management did not clarify the Rs 848 crore treasury segment profit figure on the call and said it would respond offline.
summary.management_tone: Confident on headline delivery, with management repeatedly stressing that FY26 results beat guidance. Defensive on the FY27 guidance and SMA questions, where it attributed changes to the February day-count effect and to the bank's conservative pricing, not to stress.
key_quotes: So, there is no such thing that because of this temporary crisis, we have shifted our guidance downwards.
We do not want credit growth in the Corporate segment at the cost of margins.
February impacts every financial year. SMA 2 is 60 days, but February has 28 days, while January and March have 31 days.
So, all three put together today, we are holding around Rs.1,900 crore of additional provision as a buffer towards our ECL framework.

adds.what: 110 domestic branches added in FY26 (network at 3,412 domestic branches; no further branch additions guided)

growth.why: FY27 credit growth held at 12-14% and deposits at 10-12%; backing is a Rs 14,000 crore corporate pipeline that management says it will not fund at the cost of margins, plus RAM share targets of 62-65%, with no specific new capacity or orders quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Fee income rose 32% to Rs 516 crore and cost-to-income fell 581 bps to 52.66%, and ROA is targeted at 0.95-1% from 0.87%; against that, global NIM guidance is 2.8-2.9% and CD ratio is rising to 80.21%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Network stands at 3,412 domestic branches after 110 added in FY26, with no further branch additions guided; the FY27 spend is on IT and back-office, not new physical capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Credit growth guidance of 12-14% and deposit growth of 10-12% imply continued expansion from a 19.44% advance growth base in FY26, backed by RAM growth of 24%+ and a Rs 14,000 crore corporate pipeline.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex discussion is limited to IT (FY27 budget above Rs 1,000 crore vs Rs 899 crore in FY26) and no utilisation figure or new plant was disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Credit grew 19.44% in FY26 against 12-14% FY27 guidance, and management called the guide conservative, but corporate disbursements are held back by pricing on a Rs 14,000 crore pipeline.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Credit growth guidance of 12-14% sits well below the 19.44% delivered in FY26, and the Rs 160 crore residual PLI payment and unquantified Labour Code effect could pressure employee costs; the risk is more that guidance is conservative than that it is cut.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management has a dated FY27 plan for omnichannel mobile banking, cash management, supply chain finance, forex and prepaid cards, and e-notes, following completed CBDC app and Murex treasury projects.

rows.label: Corporate loan pricing discipline
rows.why: Management will not grow corporate credit at the cost of margins, so the Rs 14,000 crore pipeline converts only if pricing clears, which caps credit growth near the 12-14% guide.

rows.label: Asset quality and recovery target
rows.why: Gross NPA is at 2.17% against a sub-2% FY27 target, and the recovery and upgradation target is Rs 2,000-2,500 crore against about Rs 1,300 crore recovered from written-off accounts in FY26.

rows.label: QIP after AGM approval
rows.why: The Board has approved a QIP, but the launch needs AGM approval and waits for market conditions; there is no plan to raise this quarter.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 delivery, ROA path and recoveries, but defensive on the FY27 guidance and the SMA 1 rise to Rs 651 crore from Rs 260 crore, and it left the Rs 848 crore treasury segment profit figure to be clarified offline.
